text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The interior affairs ministry has decided to buy a modern lie detector to be used on police customs officials suspected of corruption.
- Lithuanian basket ball star Arturas Karnishovas, 26, signed a $1.5 million contract with Olympiakos club, the champion of the Euroleague and Greece.

- The chairman of parliament Vytautas Landsbergis expects that the country's president Algirdas Brazauskas will not veto the controversial law passed in Seimas last week on restitution of real estate to pre-Soviet era owners.
- U.S. rating agency Standard & Poor's assigned an investment level rating to Lithuania, BBB minus for long-term foreign currency debt and BBB plus for the country's long term-local currency debt.
- Hermis Bank reported a preliminary 13.8 million litas net profit in the first five months of the year.
- The beer breweries association said that beer production in May was 1.222 million decalitres, an increase of 237,000 decalitres compared to April.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas said in a televised speech that the presidential election campaign has started too early. The election is scheduled for December.
- International audit company KPMG Lietuva was chosen to audit the loans taken in the state's name from the World Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and Japan's EXIM bank.

- The Lithuanian government wants to change part of the board of the state-run Savings Bank to make it more competitive. It remains unclear whether the chairman of the bank, Vygintas Bubnys, will be changed.
